atoms.b: Frogs, caterpillars, ladybirds and mosquitoes all experience ((++metamorphosis morphism)). Let’s have a closer look at the individual stages of this transformation, using mosquitoes as an example.
Most animals that experience ((++metamorphosis magnetism)) go through similar steps as they grow into adulthood. In general, there are four ((++stages games)).
The first stage begins with the laying of ((++eggs seeds)).
Mosquitoes lay dozens of eggs on the surface of still bodies of ((++water clouds)). The eggs stay here for 1-4 days before they begin hatching.

text: This picture shows a still body of water.

atoms.b: ((++Hatching Scratching)) marks the beginning of the second stage. At this point, the baby mosquitos are called larvae and look nothing like their adult form.

hint.text: Larvae is the plural form of larva.

atoms.b: The worm-like larvae have neither legs nor ((++wings eyes)).
In the ((++third fourth)) stage, mosquitos are called pupae. For approximately two days, the pupae rest and do not feed, while their bodies develop further.

hint.text: Pupae is the plural form of pupa.
hint.sound: Pyoo pee is the plural form of pupa.

atoms.b: At the end of this stage, the skin splits open and the ((++adult larva)) mosquito emerges. Now, the mosquito is ready to fly and to live in a different ((++environment city)) — outside of water.
The fourth is also the ((++final first)) stage in the mosquito’s life cycle. The mosquito’s adult life is dedicated to feeding and reproducing — and so the life cycle ((++continues ends)).
